input_signals.name: Intangible Operating Leverage
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 1)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms experiencing operating-margin expansion earn higher subsequent returns because scalable intangible assets are beginning to generate incremental rents.
input_signals.reasoning: Margin change replaces the previously weak static margin level and tests the operating-scalability mechanism directly. Intangible intensity determines the economic relevance of that expansion, while treating an absent balance-sheet intangible balance as zero preserves coverage without imputing productivity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( mul( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), delta( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 1 ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Organic-versus-Acquired Adjusted Return
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating returns after reversing R&D expensing and conservatively charging acquisition goodwill earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D to operating income treats organic knowledge creation as investment, while the goodwill-augmented denominator penalizes recognized acquisition premiums. The expression is monotone in operating income and R&D, decreases with goodwill, and remains defined for firms reporting no R&D or goodwill.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( at, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill-Loaded Cash Return
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating strong current operating cash returns after conservatively accounting for acquisition goodwill earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The denominator places an additional charge on acquisition premiums, so a high score requires cash profitability sufficient to validate the goodwill-loaded capital base. Using the current goodwill stock instead of its change avoids the acquisition-growth anomaly, reporting-transition artifacts, and the zero mass created by a positive-change indicator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( oancf, add( at, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Pre-Advertising Operating Margin
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, xad), sale), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high operating profitability after reversing the accounting expense for current brand investment earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding advertising back to operating income directly estimates the operating surplus generated before expensed brand building rather than multiplying two anomaly signals. The construction is monotone in both reported operating income and advertising, uses no unstable advertising denominator, and requires no lagged disclosure history.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( oiadp, xad ), sale ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Intangible Accumulation
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(MAX(DELTA(intan, 1), 0), ADD(at, MAX(DELTA(intan, 1), 0))), RATIO(SUB(oancf, MAX(DELTA(intan, 1), 0)), ADD(ABS(oancf), MAX(DELTA(intan, 1), 0)))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms making material additions to recorded intangible assets while generating enough operating cash flow to fund those additions earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The first term measures positive intangible accumulation, while the bounded second term distinguishes internally financed investment from accumulation exceeding operating cash generation. Using observed changes without coalescing avoids manufacturing investment when an intangible balance merely begins to be reported.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( mul( ratio( max( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ), add( at, max( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ) ) ), ratio( sub( oancf, max( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ) ), add( abs( oancf ), max( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill SG&A Synergy
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(xsga, sale), 1))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill-heavy firms realizing declining SG&A costs per dollar of sales earn higher subsequent returns as acquisition integration produces operating synergies.
input_signals.reasoning: Falling SG&A intensity measures a specific integration channel rather than relabeling operating-margin improvement. Scaling the cost reduction by goodwill intensity makes it economically relevant only where acquired businesses and their expected synergies are material.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( mul( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), neg( delta( ratio( xsga, sale ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Validated Organic Return
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose R&D-adjusted profitability is supported by both operating income and operating cash flow earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D back reverses the treatment of organic investment as a current expense, while the goodwill-loaded denominator conservatively charges recognized acquisition capital. Taking the lower adjusted profit measure requires cash and accrual profitability to agree, reducing extreme scores caused by either aggressive accruals or transitory cash flows.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( min( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ) ), add( at, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Margin Breakout
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), SUB(RATIO(oiadp, sale), LAG(TS_MAX(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3), 1))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms whose current operating margin exceeds its prior historical peak earn higher subsequent returns as intangible investment enters a commercialization regime.
input_signals.reasoning: The distance above the prior three-period maximum identifies a margin breakout rather than another one-period profitability change. Scaling that breakout by intangible intensity tests whether a commercialization milestone is more informative when nonphysical assets are economically material.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( mul( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), sub( ratio( oiadp, sale ), lag( ts_max( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Organic Intangible Equity Productivity
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ABS(ceq), COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating high R&D-adjusted income relative to a goodwill-adjusted shareholder capital base earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D back to net income corrects the immediate expensing of organic knowledge investment, while goodwill is charged against the equity capital supporting acquired intangibles. This tests productivity from the shareholder-claim perspective rather than reconstructing the published total intangible-capital denominator or repeating an asset-based return measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( abs( ceq ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Acquired Franchise Cash Margin
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, ADD(sale, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating strong operating cash flow relative to both current commercial activity and acquisition goodwill earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales represent the current revenue platform, while goodwill adds the acquisition premium that the platform must economically support. This measures cash monetization of an acquired franchise rather than smoothing the archived goodwill-loaded asset return, and it requires no temporal history.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( oancf, add( sale, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Maintenance Cash Surplus
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), ADD(sale, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating substantial operating cash flow after reserving for maintenance of an intangible-adjusted commercial platform earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Depreciation and amortization provide a conservative proxy for the recurring investment needed to maintain the productive asset base, so operating cash flow less that reserve measures distributable operating surplus. Scaling by sales plus recorded intangibles tests platform maintenance capacity rather than substituting cash flow into an existing equity-return formula.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), add( sale, coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Uncovered Goodwill Burden
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), MAX(oiadp, 0)), at), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose acquisition goodwill substantially exceeds current positive operating income earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Current positive operating income offsets the goodwill balance, so the signal measures the portion of the acquisition premium not covered by current operating profitability. Unlike another goodwill-scaled profitability ratio, this directly identifies an unvalidated acquisition burden and assigns a clear negative sign.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), max( oiadp, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Research-Reclassified Platform Efficiency
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(sale, ADD(MAX(SUB(xsga, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms producing strong pre-R&D operating surplus relative to sales, nonresearch overhead, and acquisition goodwill earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The construction reclassifies R&D from current SG&A expense to organic investment by adding it to operating income and removing it from organizational overhead. The resulting ratio measures productivity of the commercial and acquired platform after separating research investment from recurring operating costs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( sale, add( max( sub( xsga, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: After-Tax Organic Rent Retention
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ni, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ABS(ni), ADD(ABS(pi), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0))))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms retaining strong after-tax earnings after recognizing organic research investment and acquisition goodwill earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Net income plus R&D estimates after-tax earnings before research expensing, while the denominator normalizes that surplus by current after-tax and pretax income scales plus organic and acquired intangible commitments. The bounded construction tests retention of intangible rents without adding an earnings-growth anomaly to the archived equity-productivity signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( ni, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( abs( ni ), add( abs( pi ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Balanced Franchise Validation
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(SUMRANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(sale, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), RATIO(DELTA(oiadp, 1), ADD(sale, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquired franchises combining strong current cash profitability with improving operating earnings earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The two channels address complementary evidence: cash profitability supplied the strong cross-sectional level effect, while operating-income improvement generated reliable portfolio alpha. SUMRANK equalizes their cross-sectional scales, preventing the much larger cash-flow level from mechanically overwhelming the integration-improvement channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( sumrank( ratio( oancf, add( sale, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), ratio( delta( oiadp, 1 ), add( sale, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Balanced Organic Productivity
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), RATIO(DELTA(oiadp, 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(oiadp, 1)), COALESCE(xrd, 0))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms exhibiting both high current R&D-adjusted profitability and strong realized earnings conversion from research investment earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The first channel measures the level of organic intangible productivity, while the second measures marginal commercialization through operating-income improvement. Rank balancing prevents the stronger profitability level from erasing the independently reliable portfolio information in research conversion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( sumrank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( at, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), mul( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), add( at, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), ratio( delta( oiadp, 1 ), add( abs( delta( oiadp, 1 ) ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maintenance-Validated After-Tax Rent
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(ADD(ni, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), SUB(oancf, dp)), ADD(at, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose R&D-adjusted after-tax earnings are supported by maintenance-adjusted operating cash flow earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Net income plus R&D estimates after-tax organic rents, while operating cash flow less depreciation provides a conservative distributable-cash measure after reserving for asset maintenance. Taking the lower amount identifies earnings that survive both tax and maintenance hurdles rather than combining two portfolio ranks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( min( add( ni, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), sub( oancf, dp ) ), add( at, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Confirmed Intangible Breakout
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(SUMRANK(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), SUB(RATIO(oiadp, sale), LAG(TS_MAX(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3), 1))), RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), ADD(sale, COALESCE(intan, 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive margin milestones accompanied by strong maintenance-adjusted cash profitability predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The first channel detects commercialization relative to the firm’s prior margin peak, while the second requires the platform to generate cash after a maintenance reserve. Rank balancing prevents either the margin gap or cash-profitability scale from dominating and may improve the breakout signal’s portfolio stability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( sumrank( mul( ratio( coalesce( intan, 0 ), at ), sub( ratio( oiadp, sale ), lag( ts_max( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ), ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), add( sale, coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Residual-Goodwill Organic Return
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, MAX(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), MAX(oiadp, 0)), 0))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating high R&D-adjusted operating returns after charging only the portion of goodwill unsupported by current operating income earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Current positive operating income first covers acquisition goodwill, and only the residual uncovered premium expands the productive capital base. The numerator then measures organic profitability before R&D expensing, creating a nonlinear interaction between acquisition validation and organic intangible productivity rather than a rank blend.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( at, max( sub( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), max( oiadp, 0 ) ), 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Shareholder-Franchise Cash Validation
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ABS(ceq), COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), RATIO(oancf, ADD(sale, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high R&D-adjusted shareholder earnings and strong cash generation from their goodwill-adjusted commercial franchise earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The equity-productivity channel measures organic rents accruing to shareholders, while the franchise-cash channel validates their realization through current commercial activity. Their different numerators and capital scalers provide complementary evidence rather than two transformations of the same profitability ratio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( sumrank( ratio( add( ib, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( abs( ceq ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), ratio( oancf, add( sale, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Research Program Return
input_signals.expression: IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ADD(sale, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(sale, VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high pre-R&D operating profitability and stable research intensity earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D back measures operating surplus before organic knowledge investment, while the dollar-scaled volatility of R&D intensity imposes a hurdle for unstable or episodic research programs. This tests research-program continuity rather than reusing the archived research-conversion or margin-breakout channels.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( add( sale, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), mul( sale, vol( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Uncovered Intangible Investment

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose positive additions to recorded intangible assets exceed current positive operating income earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Current operating income offsets new intangible investment dollar for dollar, leaving an uncovered investment amount rather than a generic asset-growth measure. The construction uses observed intangible changes without coalescing, avoiding artificial investment events caused by firms beginning to report the balance.

input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( max( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ), max( oiadp, 0 ) ), add( at, max( delta( intan, 1 ), 0 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.reasoning: Current positive cash generation first covers the acquisition premium, leaving only residual goodwill as an additional claim on shareholder capital. input_signals.reasoning: The minimum operator measures only the portion of current research spending covered by positive operating cash generation, so neither unfunded R&D nor cash flow without research receives full credit.
